RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-A0D25E0D66-82168
Member: Skyler Alvarez, Member ID W468430798
Date of Notice: 2026-08-05
Requested Service: Lumbar disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
Treating Surgeon: Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 (lumbar laminotomy/decompression with excision of herniated intervertebral disc), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-05. This appeal is submitted within the 180-calendar-day deadline stated in that notice (by 2027-02-01).

**1. The stated denial reason is not supported by the clinical record.**

The notice states that the request was denied because "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." The record submitted with the prior authorization request, and summarized below, documents a sustained and multi-modal course of conservative treatment that was unsuccessful:

- **Duration of symptoms:** 12 months of progressive low back pain unrelieved by rest.
- **Supervised physical therapy:** 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy (core stabilization and lumbar flexibility), 18 completed visits, from 2026-04-04 through 2026-07-11, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- **Interventional treatment:** Corticosteroid (epidural) injection administered 2026-04-29, yielding only approximately 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging confirmation:** MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-07-06 showing an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- **Functional impact:** Patient is unable to stand more than 10 minutes and has radicular pain radiating into the right calf.
- **Exam findings:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level of compression.
- **No contraindications:** No active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, BMI 29, non-smoker.

Taken together, these records show conservative care well in excess of what is typically required before proceeding to surgical decompression — including physical therapy, activity modification implicit in the PT program, sustained NSAID use, and an epidural steroid injection — combined with an imaging-confirmed structural lesion and an objective neurologic deficit. We ask that the plan reverse the denial and identify, specifically, what additional conservative treatment element it believes is missing, given the above.

**2. Regarding the applicable medical-necessity criteria.**

In researching this appeal, we identified that Centene Corporation (the parent organization of Peach State Health Plan/Ambetter) publishes a clinical policy titled "Disc Decompression Procedures," Reference Number CP.MP.114. That policy states, in relevant part:

"It is the policy of health plans affiliated with Centene Corporation® that open discectomy and microdiscectomy are medically necessary when meeting all of the following: A. Age ≥ 18 years; B. Diagnosis of herniated lumbar disc; C. Nerve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following: 1. Radiculopathy with motor deficit and one of the following: ... b. Mild to moderate weakness in a nerve root distribution, as evidenced by a score of 4 on the MRC 0 to 5 muscle strength scale and one of the following: i. Worsening weakness or motor deficit; ii. Member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative therapy, within the last year, including all of the following: a) ≥ four weeks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee's inability to tolerate; b) ≥ four weeks activity modification; c) One of the following: 1) Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) or acetaminophen ≥ three weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated; 2) Epidural steroid injection; 2. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution, and member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative therapy including all the following: a. ≥ four weeks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee's inability to tolerate; b. ≥ four weeks activity modification; c. One of the following: i. NSAID or acetaminophen ≥ three weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated; ii. Epidural steroid injection."

The conservative-therapy record above (14 weeks of PT, 8 months of NSAIDs, an epidural steroid injection, all within the last year) exceeds each of the numeric thresholds quoted above (≥4 weeks PT, ≥3 weeks NSAID/acetaminophen, and an epidural steroid injection).

However, we want to be transparent with the plan: we could not confirm that CP.MP.114 is in fact the specific document used to review this member's CPT 63030 request. That policy's own coding tables do not list CPT 63030 among the codes it applies to, and Ambetter from Peach State Health Plan has publicly stated that utilization management and medical-necessity review for spine surgical procedures — including "Laminectomy/discectomy" and "spinal decompression" — has been delegated to TurningPoint Healthcare Solutions, LLC. We were not able to obtain the text of TurningPoint's internal clinical guideline for this procedure; TurningPoint has indicated that such criteria are provided only on request or through a secure provider portal.

**We therefore also request, as part of this appeal, that the plan and/or TurningPoint identify the exact clinical policy or guideline (title, reference number, and effective/revision date) actually applied to this member's CPT 63030 request, and provide us with its full medical-necessity criteria text, so that the record can be evaluated against the correct standard.** If the criteria differ from those quoted above from CP.MP.114, we ask for the opportunity to supplement this appeal with any additional documentation responsive to those specific criteria.

**3. Requested action.**

Based on the documented 12-month symptom history, the completed and unsuccessful conservative treatment (physical therapy, prolonged NSAID use, and epidural steroid injection), the MRI-confirmed L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe lateral recess stenosis and nerve root compression, and the corresponding neurologic deficit and functional limitation, we respectfully request that the plan:

1. Reverse the denial of CPT 63030 and approve the requested lumbar decompression/discectomy; or, in the alternative,
2. Disclose the specific medical-necessity policy and criteria actually applied to this request, so that any remaining documentation gap can be addressed; and
3. Given the patient's significant functional limitation (unable to stand more than 10 minutes) and radicular symptoms, treat this appeal as requiring expedited handling if the plan's standard timeframe would result in a delay detrimental to the patient's health, and advise us of the applicable expedited appeal procedure and timeframe.

Enclosed with this appeal are copies of: the physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-04 to 2026-07-11), medication/pharmacy records documenting the NSAID trial, the procedure note for the corticosteroid injection dated 2026-04-29, the MRI report dated 2026-07-06, and the treating surgeon's clinical notes documenting the neurologic examination findings, Dr. Marchetti's operative recommendation, and the original prior authorization request.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and provide the name and direct contact information of the individual or department handling this appeal. If any additional information is needed to complete the review, please contact me at the phone number or email address above, or contact Dr. Marchetti's office at [surgeon office phone/fax].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Skyler Alvarez
